# Web front end

Applies when the change touches: HTML, CSS, browser code. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WCAG AA | 2.2 (published 2024-12-12); W3C Recommendation; this is its current dated version | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/> |
| Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) | 2024 thresholds | 2026-09-28 | <https://web.dev/articles/vitals> |
| Content Security Policy | Level 2 (W3C Recommendation, 2016), with the Level 3 features every engine ships: nonces and strict-dynamic | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/> |

| OWASP Cheat Sheet Series (XSS, CSRF, clickjacking) | current | 2026-09-28 | <https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/> |
| Every state a reviewer cannot navigate to is a state the developer will invent: fixture-driven state switching, and a stable `data-testid` on every interactive element so the tester can drive the prototype with Playwright | — | 2026-09-25 (reviewed) | — |
| W3C ACT Rules as the machine-checkable form of a WCAG success criterion | ACT Rules Format 1.1; WCAG 2.2 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/act/rules/> |
| OWASP Developer Guide secure coding checklists (successor of the archived Secure Coding Practices Quick Reference Guide), and abuse cases derived by the OWASP Abuse Case and Attack Surface Analysis method | OWASP Developer Guide, current living release (updated through 2023 and 2024); The Secure Coding Practices Quick-reference Guide v2.1 is archived; its checklists moved into the Developer Guide | 2026-09-28 | <https://owasp.org/www-project-developer-guide/> |
| EN 301 549 accessibility requirements for ICT products and services | V4.1.1 (published 2026-09-02); prepared for Directive (EU) 2019/882; V3.2.1 (2021-03) remains the version cited in the Official Journal until V4.1.1 is | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/04.01.01_60/en_301549v040101p.pdf> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Name the pages, components, and states the change touches; a user-facing change needs the product designer and `design.files`. |
| Specify | Acceptance names every state per screen (empty, loading, error, partial, success, offline) and the keyboard path through it. |
| Specify | Performance budgets in the Acceptance: LCP, INP, and CLS thresholds for the pages touched. |
| Implement | Semantic HTML first, ARIA only where HTML has no element; focus order and a visible focus ring preserved. |
| Implement | No inline script and no `unsafe-inline`: nonces or hashes under the CSP; every third-party script named in the Spec. |
| Review | Untrusted strings reach the DOM only through escaping or a sanitizer; URLs are validated before `href` or `src`. |
| Ship | Core Web Vitals field data and the client error rate are the observe signals. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| axe-core | no WCAG 2.2 A or AA violation on any screen state | `@axe-core/cli` or axe in Playwright, one run per state |
| Lighthouse CI | the LCP, INP, CLS, and bundle-size budgets hold | `lhci autorun` with a budget file |
| Visual regression | no unreviewed visual change per state | Playwright screenshots against the baseline frozen at Spec approval |
| CSP evaluation | no `unsafe-inline` and no wildcard source in the policy | Google CSP Evaluator or a lint step in CI |
| ESLint with jsx-a11y and security plugins | no accessibility or injection anti-pattern in the code | `eslint` in the test commands |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
